title: Treating AI transformation as an IT project or one person’s responsibility
summary: Join executive sponsorship, process ownership and technical delivery without pretending one role can do all three.
diagnosis: A technical team can build a service without having authority to resolve business priorities, change incentives or assign responsibility across departments. An executive sponsor can create urgency without owning day-to-day decisions. State which decisions sit with the sponsor, the process owner and the operational owner; give each the resources needed to carry that responsibility.
diagnostic_questions: Who can make cross-functional tradeoffs about the outcome, risk and workflow design?
Does the named owner have authority and time, or only accountability after a failure?
Which responsibilities would be uncovered if the AI specialist or sponsor left tomorrow?
proposed_actions: Name a business outcome owner, an executive escalation route and a delivery/operating owner for each initiative.
Write decision rights for prioritisation, data access, acceptance, release, budget and exceptions; include affected functions rather than a ceremonial steering group.
Review whether management work has genuinely disappeared or has moved into informal coordination, coaching and conflict resolution.
working_artifact: Responsibility and decision-rights map: outcome sponsor; process owner; technical owner; data owner; risk approver; operational responder; decision scope; available resources; escalation route; deputy.
measures: Time taken to resolve cross-functional decisions blocking delivery.
Share of live workflows with an empowered outcome owner and an operational owner, measured separately.
Unresolved decisions and recurring escalations caused by ambiguous authority, not simply meeting attendance.
tradeoff: There is no universally correct flat or centralised structure. Removing a management layer does not remove the need for judgement, coaching or accountability. A small company may combine roles, but should not leave their duties implicit.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: an engineer can build a sales assistant, but only the business can decide whose pipeline definition applies, what advice a manager must review and how saved time changes account coverage.
